issue_description.description: The audit traced each supplement filter through selection, section visibility, evidence updates, notice visibility, category-top ownership, table-of-contents rebuilding, and information-only mode. It checked the responsive CSS and measured the rendered document and every filter button at 320, 360, 390, 412, and 539 pixel viewports. It also traced the Blog page metadata and heading to the /blog/ route-registry entry, and reviewed the visual harness sequence that waits for document fonts, prepares state, and waits for visible images before capture. The focused unit and Chromium tests passed. No defect was reproduced or supported by the reviewed code. The audit did not assess unrelated migration features, production infrastructure, or the already documented visual-parity exceptions.
issue_description.code_example:
Evidence checked:
- Focused Vitest result: 2 files passed, 5 tests passed. - Focused Chromium result: 6 supplement and Blog tests passed. - Mobile Chromium result: the supplement notice, category-top, and overflow test passed. - Explicit responsive probe: document scroll width matched client width at 320, 360, 390, 412, and 539 pixels; all filter buttons remained inside the viewport; information-only mode retained exactly one category-top target.
